edits.content:
# L04 closure: checkpoint attachment binding

## Decision

Persistent checkpoint attachments are represented as five closed kinds of restricted references: `task-attachment`, `recovery-instruction`, `context`, `external-artifact-ref`, and `ledger-checkpoint`. No arbitrary cursor or blob is admitted to the recovered set.

A recovered binding consists of kind, reference, SHA-256 content hash, owner, and TTL/expiry. Content may be presented to the validator to prove the hash, but content is never copied into the binding output.

## Validation and repair

The recovery validator turns invalid candidates into explicit status entries:

- `missing-hash` and `invalid-hash`;
- `missing-owner`;
- `missing-ttl` and `expired`;
- `missing-ref` and `invalid-kind`;
- `conflict`.

Only candidates that pass all checks appear in `recovered`. If the same attachment reference carries different hashes, the first binding remains authoritative and later candidates receive `conflict`. Identical kind/reference/hash candidates are deduplicated and do not produce additional recovered bindings.

## Purity and reproducibility

The runtime implementation performs no I/O and invokes no side effect. It reads the candidate collection without modifying it. Sorting and canonical serialization make output independent of candidate order. A supplied `now` allows completely deterministic expiry tests. The returned digest covers the normalized recovered and excluded collections and can be recomputed with `digestCheckpointAttachmentBindingRecovery`.

## Verification expectations

The closure is complete when runtime-core type checks and scoped lint pass; targeted candidate tests cover all five kinds and each repair state; harness validation and dry-run pass; communication replay/compare remains unchanged; the credential scan reports zero findings; and repository `SHA256SUMS` can be read and verified.
